uncited: The Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function (BRDF) is a 4D function that describes how light is reflected at an opaque surface, serving as the core component of the surface rendering equation.

It defines the ratio of reflected radiance in a specific outgoing direction to the incident irradiance from a specific incoming direction, thereby modeling the angular distribution of reflected light.

It is distinguished from its sibling [Bidirectional Transmittance Distribution Function (BTDF)](52-btdf.md) by modeling reflection rather than transmission, and from [Bidirectional Scattering Surface Reflectance Distribution Function (BSSRDF)](52-bssrdf.md) by assuming light does not penetrate the surface volume.
The concept of the BRDF was formalized in the context of computer graphics to provide a rigorous mathematical framework for surface shading.
It builds upon the [Surface Rendering Equation](14578-surface-rendering-equation.md), which defines the boundary condition for light transport.
The model assumes opaque surfaces where light interaction is confined to the surface interface, distinguishing it from volume-based scattering models.
